title: Resurrection of Type IIL Supernova 2018ivc: Implications for a Binary Evolution Sequence Connecting Hydrogen-rich and Hydrogen-poor Progenitors
question: What is the late-time (>1,000 days) millimeter synchrotron evolution of the peculiar Type IIL supernova SN 2018ivc, and what does the outer circumstellar matter (CSM) distribution reveal about the progenitor's mass-loss history in the final millennium before the explosion and its binary evolution pathway?

data.angular_resolution: DDT (2021.A.00026.S): 0.81'' x 0.71'' (avg 0.76'') in Band 3 and 0.33'' x 0.28'' (avg 0.30'') in Band 6; across all epochs: 0.05'' to 1.17'' in Band 3 and 0.03'' to 0.50'' in Band 6

what.value: Early-phase ALMA Band 3 and Band 6 flux measurements and SED slope at days 4.1 to 198.6

Maeda), complemented by the data at earlier epochs published in (cite: maeda_2018ivc) and archival data newly presented in this work.

what.value: Centimeter flux measurements at 6.5 GHz (VLA) and 6.3 GHz (e-MERLIN) on day 1,217 (~1,000 days after the explosion)

evidence.quote: Recently, its detection at $\sim 1,000$ days after the explosion in the *cm* emission, at 6.5 GHz by the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA) and at 6.3 GHz by the enhanced Multi-Element Radio Linked Interferometer Network (e-MERLIN), was reported (cite: mutie2022).
Fig. [2](#fig:sed) compares the Spectral Energy Distribution (SED) on days 199 and 1,364 , with the addition of the *cm* flux on day 1,217 taken from (cite: mutie2022).

what.value: Upper limit on the main-sequence mass of a single star progenitor (<= 11 M_sun) from pre-SN Hubble Space Telescope images

evidence.quote: (cite: bostroem2020) placed an upper limit of the MS mass of a ‘single star’ being $\mathrel{lap{\lower 4pt \hbox{\hskip 1pt $\sim$}}aise 1pt \hbox {$<$}}11 M_\odot$ that existed at the SN location in pre-SN Hubble Space Telescope images.

recipe.goal: Calibrate, image, and select ALMA continuum observations
recipe.method: Use standard ALMA pipeline calibrated data for DDT program; download processed continuum FITS images from JVO for archival Band 3 programs with SN S/N > 5; manually image 2018.1.01135.S and 2019.1.00026.S using CASA clean with primary beam correction (and self-calibration for 2018.1.01135.S).
key_parameters: S/N > 5 selection threshold for archival Band 3 data

recipe.goal: Measure continuum flux densities and spectral index
recipe.method: Measure continuum flux densities associated with the SN on each image using the imfit task in CASA, and compute the spectral energy distribution slope assuming a power law.
assumptions: Power-law spectral energy distribution f_nu proportional to nu^alpha

recipe.goal: Model synchrotron light curves and constrain CSM density distribution and mass-loss history
recipe.method: Compute synchrotron emission models for SN-CSM interaction after ~500 days by varying the outer CSM power-law density slope s and density scale D, and compare the resulting radial CSM density and mass-loss history to binary evolution models.
key_parameters: Outer CSM inner radius ~ 4 x 10^16 cm (interaction epoch >= 500 days)
assumptions: Ejecta mass M_ej = 3 M_sun, kinetic energy E_K = 1.2 x 10^51 erg, outer ejecta density slope n = -10
CSM density profile rho_CSM proportional to D r^-s without an inner hole in the computation
SN shock velocity ~ 10,000 km s^-1 and CSM wind velocity v_w ~ 20 km s^-1

Band 3 continuum flux density at day 213.5 (MJD 58658.5, 92.1 GHz)

evidence.quote: Given the SED slope of $\alpha = -1.12 \pm  0.22$ on day 199 (cite: maeda_2018ivc), there is a hint of the spectral steepening but it is also consistent with no change within $1\sigma$ (i.e., $\alpha = -1.22 \pm 0.27$ for the combined analysis of the data on days 199 and 1,364).

While there is a degeneracy in the CSM slope given the limited temporal coverage, the CSM density at $\sim 10^{17}$ cm is strongly constrained to be $\sim 10^{-18}$ g cm$^{-3}$; this is where the data points exist.

answer_key.quantity: Progenitor mass-loss rate at ~ 1,500 years before explosion

evidence.quote: We find that the progenitor of SN 2018ivc had experienced a very high mass-loss rate ($\mathrel{lap{\lower 4pt \hbox{\hskip 1pt $\sim$}}aise 1pt \hbox {$>$}}10^{-3} M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$) $\sim 1,500$ years before the explosion, which was followed by a moderately high mass-loss rate ($\mathrel{lap{\lower 4pt \hbox{\hskip 1pt $\sim$}}aise 1pt \hbox {$>$}}10^{-4} M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$) up until the explosion.

answer_key.quantity: Progenitor mass-loss rate in remaining evolution up until explosion

evidence.quote: We find that the progenitor of SN 2018ivc had experienced a very high mass-loss rate ($\mathrel{lap{\lower 4pt \hbox{\hskip 1pt $\sim$}}aise 1pt \hbox {$>$}}10^{-3} M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$) $\sim 1,500$ years before the explosion, which was followed by a moderately high mass-loss rate ($\mathrel{lap{\lower 4pt \hbox{\hskip 1pt $\sim$}}aise 1pt \hbox {$>$}}10^{-4} M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$) up until the explosion.
The models presented here suggest that $\sim 1 M_\odot$ of the CSM has been swept up by day $\sim 1,500$.

score_reason: The ALMA observational measurements (point-source continuum flux densities via CASA imfit) are straightforward to reproduce from public archive/JVO data (+2 data, +2 reduction, +1 completeness), with main numeric flux and spectral index results clearly tabulated (+1), though the custom synchrotron light-curve code and some imaging/microphysics parameters are not self-contained in the text.
rediscovery_reason: All seven ALMA datasets are public in the archive (and mostly available as processed continuum FITS images via JVO/ALMA archive), the point-source flux measurements with CASA imfit and power-law spectral index calculation are simple and unambiguous, and the main observational claims rely directly on the numeric flux densities in Table 1.
